CA	The Category Administrator of the Championship as appointed by the CM .
Championship	The 2026 Porsche Equity-One Carrera Cup Australia Championship.
CM	The Category Manager of the Championship as appointed by Motorsport Australia .
Code of Driving Conduct	A document detailing the minimum level of conduct expected by all Drivers as published by Motorsport Australia .
Control Component	A component that is specified for use in the Championship and is supplied by PAG or a Control Component Supplier . Unless otherwise stated in these regulations, the fitment and/or use of each Control Component is mandatory.
Control Component Service Agent	The agent permitted to service a Control Component as nominated by the CM .
Control Component Supplier	The manufacturer and/or supplier of a Control Component as nominated by the CM .
CRSR	Circuit Race Standing Regulations as promulgated by Motorsport Australia .
DM	The Driver Mentor as appointed by the CM .
DRD	The Deputy Race Director as appointed by Motorsport Australia .
DSA	The Driving Standards Advisor as appointed by Motorsport Australia .
FIA	The Federation Internationale de l'Automobile.
Guest Driver	An eligible Driver that is invited by the CM to compete at a Round .
Joker Tyre	A Tyre that has been manufactured by Michelin and supplied by the nominated Control Component Supplier , that has not been used or modified in any way, and is permitted to be used in practice in accordance with Regulation S16.3.
Marked Tyre	A Tyre that has been approved for use in the Championship by the TD .
OM	The Operations Manager as appointed by the CM .
Organiser	The organiser of a Round as advised in the Supplementary Regulations issued for an event.
PAG	Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche Aktiengesellschaft
Paddock	A defined area within the Precinct , designated for the garaging of Automobiles and associated equipment.
Precinct	The area within the perimeter of the event venue.
Previously Marked Tyre	A Marked Tyre from a prior Round that is approved for use by a specific Driver .
Previously Used Brake Rotor	A brake rotor that has at least 0.2 mm of wear, measured adjacent to the wear indicators on the brake rotor.
Racing Weight	The weight of an Automobile (including safety gear and liquids) and its Driver (including apparel) at any time during a Competition , such as at the end of practice, qualifying or a race.
RD	The Race Director as appointed by Motorsport Australia .
RMC	Race Management Channel.
Round	A round of the Championship .

One stint is equivalent to the mileage indicated (including a maximum of 2 pit stops and/or driving under pace car). At this mileage and this speed limit, the integrity of the construction is guaranteed for endurance but not for wear potential or grip potential. Therefore, depending on the conditions of use, a tyre :

Could be worn before achieving the indicated mileage,

Could be only partially  worn  even  though  the  indicated  mileage  has  been  achieved.  In  this case, the integrity of the construction cannot be guaranteed, the tyre must be replaced.

Incorrectly adjusted camber and tyre pressure values can cause tyre failure.

Respect the specified camber and tyre pressure values listed in the Michelin Precos (Porsche Technical recommendations N3_N3R_2025.pdf)).

For circuits not listed in the Michelin Precos, the specifications for 'low stress circuit standard' must be used.

Exceeding the maximum camber shim thickness for the corresponding circuit type is not permitted.
At all times, each Automobile must achieve a minimum Racing Weight of 1385 kg.

At all times each Driver must weigh a minimum of 85 kg (including all normal racing apparel in accordance with Technical Appendix -Schedule D).

If a Driver weighs less than 85 kg, Driver ballast must be affixed to the Automobile to achieve the minimum Driver Weight.

From the time an Automobile leaves its garage prior to the commencement of a Track session, until the time the Automobile is released from Parc Fermé after the session, the Automobile must have a minimum of 2.0 kg of fuel in its fuel system, capable of being extracted from the fuel sampling point.

During the Championship each Driver will be permitted to use a maximum of six (6) front and six (6) rear Joker Tyres .

At each Round, each Driver is permitted to use a maximum of two (2) front and two (2) rear Joker Tyres .

If a Driver wishes to use Joker Tyres at any Round , the Competitor must:

Place an order for Joker Tyres with the Control Component Supplier at least seven (7) days prior to the commencement of the Round in which the Joker Tyres are to be used, and;

Notify the TD at least sixty (60) minutes prior to the scheduled start time of the practice session in which the Joker Tyres are to be used.

Only use the supplied Map Switch.

Do not exceed the max. tightening torque of 1 to 2 Nm. Overtorquing can damage the switch or make it difficult to turn.

Remove the front cover of the switch to access the retaining hardware.

All hydraulic connections between ABS M5Use rigid steel brake lines with a diameter of 3.3 mm for as much of the plumbing as possible. Flexible line should be kept to an absolute minimum for optimal brake control and pedal feel.

The ABS M5 units use a DIN (bubble) flare convention common to European OEM applications. The best and simplest way to adapt the system hydraulically is with an M12x1 DIN tube nut on the ports. Tube nut size should be fitting to the hard line size used. Adapters should be avoided if possible.

The EBS unit is secured in the vehicle on the provided mounting board. During operation, the EBS unit will vibrate. These vibrations are then transferred to the brake lines. To prevent vibration-induced damage to the brake lines, they must not be secured at up to 20 cm from the EBS unit so that they can vibrate freely.

System reset after drive cycle faults.

Drive cycle faults, e.g. because of wheel speed sensor bug, need an ABS M5-ECU reset (Power off - Power on). After the reset, the car has to accelerate to more than 12 km/h for system check.

For the 12-position map switch, you can specify a default value. If the function switch fails for any reason, the switch automatically takes the position of the default value.
